title: Subject Pronouns
example: She studies English every day.

title: To be – Affirmative
example: I am a student.

title: To be – Negative & Questions
example: I am not tired.

title: Object Pronouns
formula: I→me; you→you; he→him; she→her; it→it; we→us; they→them.
example: She calls me every day.

title: Singular & Regular Plural Nouns
example: one book – two books

title: Irregular Plural Nouns
example: Two men are waiting.

title: Countable & Uncountable Nouns
formula: a/an + singular countable noun; two + plural
example: I have two apples.

title: Indefinite Articles
example: I have a pen.

title: Definite Article & Zero Article
example: I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.

title: Past Simple – To be
example: The door was locked yesterday.

title: Past Simple – Regular Verbs
example: She visited the museum on Saturday.

title: Past Simple – Irregular Verbs
example: We went to the beach yesterday.

title: Past Simple – Questions & Negatives
example: Did you finish the history project yesterday?

title: Past Time Expressions
example: I submitted the assignment yesterday.

title: Past Continuous
example: At nine last night, I was reading a detective novel.

title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
example: I was cooking dinner when the fire alarm rang.

title: Used to – Introduction
formula: S + used to + V nguyên mẫu
example: I used to walk to school, but now I take the bus.

title: Comparative – Short Adjectives
example: The library is quieter than the sports hall.

title: Comparative – Long & Irregular Adjectives
example: This dictionary is more useful than that small phrasebook.

title: Superlatives
example: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level.

title: Equality Comparisons
example: My sister is as tall as our mother now.

title: Adverbs of Manner
example: Please speak slowly so the new student can understand.

title: Future Simple – Will
example: I think it will rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella.

title: Be Going To
formula: S + am/is/are going to + V nguyên mẫu
example: I am going to study English after dinner tonight.

title: Present Continuous for Future
example: I am seeing the dentist tomorrow.

title: Will vs Going To
example: The phone is ringing. I’ll answer it.

title: Present Perfect – Experiences
example: I have visited Singapore.

title: Present Perfect – Recent Events
example: She has just left.

title: Present Perfect – Duration
example: I have lived here for five years.

group: Past Simple vs Present Perfect – Introduction
title: Past Simple vs Present Perfect – Introduction
example: I saw him yesterday.

title: Should / Shouldn't
example: You should drink water.

title: Must / Mustn't / Have to
example: You must show your ticket.

title: May / Might / Could
example: It may rain later.

title: Gerunds – Basic
example: I enjoy reading mysteries.

title: Infinitives – Basic
example: I want to learn Japanese.

title: Zero Conditional
example: If you heat ice, it melts.

title: First Conditional
formula: If + S + V(s/es), S + will + V
example: If I finish early, I will call you.

title: Time Clauses
formula: will + V + when/as soon as + S + present
example: I will call when I arrive.

title: Basic Relative Clauses
example: The man who lives next door is a chef.

title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
example: We visited the museum last Sunday.

title: Present Perfect – Duration
formula: have/has + V3 + since + mốc thời gian / mệnh đề quá khứ
example: She has lived here since 2020.

title: Present Perfect Continuous
example: We have been studying since eight.

title: Perfect Simple vs Continuous
example: She has sent six emails today so far.

title: Past Perfect
example: The film had begun when we arrived.

title: Narrative Tenses
example: The alarm rang and everybody left the room.

title: Past Habits & Familiarity
example: My grandmother used to live near the sea.

title: Future Continuous
example: At eight tomorrow, I will be studying.

title: Future Perfect
example: By Friday, they will have finished the bridge.

title: Future Time Clauses
formula: When/As soon as/After + present simple, ... will + V
example: I will call you when I arrive.

title: First Conditional – Extended
formula: If + present simple, S + will + V
example: If it rains, we will stay inside.

title: Second Conditional
formula: If + past simple, S + would + V
example: If I had more money, I would travel abroad.

title: Preferences
example: I prefer reading to watching television.

title: Wish & If Only – Present
example: I wish I had more free time.

title: Passive Voice – Present & Past
example: The rooms are cleaned every morning.

title: Passive Voice – Other Tenses
example: By the time the guests arrived, excavation findings had been documented by the archaeologist.

title: Passive Agents & Instruments
example: The paperwork for grammar rules was approved by the language tutor yesterday.

title: Defining Relative Clauses
example: The gardener's assistant who helped Owen works at the history museum.

title: Non-defining Relative Clauses
example: Owen, who works at the history museum, is speaking today about storage doors.

title: Relative Pronouns & Omission
example: In “The bicycle mechanic who led the tour was friendly”, “who” cannot be omitted because it is the clause subject.

title: Reported Statements
example: Yesterday, Owen said, “I am responsible for the report on interview clips.” Later, Owen said that he was responsible for the report on interview clips.

title: Reported Questions
example: “Do you need the report on borrowed books?” Owen asked me. I reported that Owen asked me whether I needed the report on borrowed books.

title: Reported Commands & Requests
example: The manager told Owen to check the report on ocean temperatures before lunch.

title: Indirect Questions
example: Could you tell me where the meeting is taking place near the history museum to discuss new dance steps?

title: Question Tags
example: Owen is responsible for the report on survey results, isn’t he?

title: Modals of Deduction – Present
example: During a project involving air pollution levels, all lights are on and voices are coming from the history museum. Based on this strong evidence, someone must be inside.

title: Modals – Obligation & Permission
example: Safety notice at the history museum: Visitors must not enter the restricted room storing fresh bread.

title: Gerunds & Infinitives
example: Owen enjoys reading the report on the tomato plants on the train.

title: Verb Patterns – Meaning Changes
example: Owen stopped to answer a call while walking to the history museum to collect notes on the new speakers.

title: Phrasal Verb Grammar
example: Before the presentation about an interview article, the projector was overheating, so Owen turned it off.

title: Concession
example: Although the bus was crowded, Maya gave her seat to an elderly passenger.

title: Purpose, Reason & Result
example: We postponed the picnic because dark clouds were gathering above the park.

title: Correlative Structures
formula: Both ... and – hai điều đều đúng
example: The new library offers both printed books and digital magazines.

title: Determiners
formula: Each of + danh từ số nhiều + động từ số ít
example: Each of the three candidates has a different professional background.

title: Noun Clauses – Introduction
example: I was surprised by the fact that the library had closed without notice.

title: Third Conditional
formula: If + S + had + V3, S + would have + V3
example: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.

title: Mixed Conditionals
formula: If + S + had + V3, S + would + V (now)
example: If she had taken the course, she would speak Italian now.

title: Wish & If Only – Past Regrets
example: I wish I had asked for help earlier.

title: Modal Perfects – Regret
example: After discovering the mistake, the designer admitted they should have revised the website layout sooner.

title: Modal Perfects – Deduction
example: The signed log proves that the accountant must have reconciled the monthly invoices before lunch.

title: Modal Perfects – Possibility
example: No one saw the handover; perhaps the inspector might have checked the fire exits before leaving.

title: Future Perfect Continuous
example: By the end of next month, the analyst will have been working on the sales figures for six weeks.

title: Advanced Perfect Aspect
example: At the moment the audit began, the developer had already debugged the payment system.

title: Perfect Infinitives
example: The records show that the student seems to have revised the laboratory report before the inspection.

title: Impersonal Passive Reporting
example: It is reported that the archivist has digitized the historical records ahead of schedule.

title: Personal Passive Reporting
example: The editor is said to have proofread the final chapter before the meeting.

title: Causative Structures
example: The engineer had the backup generator tested by a specialist last week.

title: Get Passive vs Be Passive
example: The survey responses got analyzed after several unexpected delays.

title: Passive with Modals & Perfect Forms
example: The website layout must be revised before the safety inspection.

title: Present Participle Clauses
example: While reconciling the monthly invoices, the accountant noticed an unexpected problem.

title: Past & Perfect Participle Clauses
example: Having verified the invoice, the accountant sent it to the team.

title: Reduced Relative Clauses
example: The document verified by the accountant was sent to the director.

title: Non-finite Clauses of Purpose & Result
example: The accountant stayed late to verify the invoice.

title: Advanced Reporting Verbs
example: The accountant promised to verify the invoice before Friday.

title: Reported Speech – Advanced
example: At the meeting, the accountant said that the team had verified the invoice the day before.

title: Future in the Past
example: At the briefing, the accountant said the team would verify the invoice on Friday.

title: Complex Noun Clauses
example: The problem is that the team may not verify the invoice on time.

title: Advanced Relative Clauses
example: The invoice, which the accountant had verified twice, was finally approved.

title: Advanced Quantifiers
example: Neither of the two drafts was ready for the accountant to verify.

title: Determiner Contrasts
example: Of the two versions, one was outdated and the other was used by the accountant.

title: Advanced Gerund & Infinitive Patterns
example: The accountant looks forward to verifying the invoice with the new team.

title: Verb Patterns – Meaning Contrasts
example: Before leaving, the accountant remembered to verify the invoice.

title: Advanced Concession
example: Despite the tight deadline, the accountant managed to verify the invoice.

title: Contrast Clauses
example: The accountant preferred to work alone, whereas the assistants wanted to verify the invoice together.

title: Result & Degree Clauses
example: The task was so complex that the accountant needed extra time to verify the invoice.

title: As If / As Though
formula: as if / as though + past simple
example: Although Leo joined only yesterday, Leo talks as though he knew everything about the library catalogue.

title: Preferences & Unreal Time
example: I would rather finalise the speaker list after lunch than rush through it now.

title: Introduction to Inversion
example: Never before has Noah seen such a confusing version of the release notes.

title: Ellipsis & Substitution
example: Linh has counted the remaining supplies, and so has the supervisor.

title: Emphasis & Cleft Sentences
example: It was Oliver who spotted the error in the inspection checklist, not the director.

title: Negative Adverbial Inversion
example: Never have we encountered such an urgent request.

title: Sequencing Inversion
formula: No sooner + had + S + V3 + than + S + V2
example: No sooner had the guests arrived than the show began.

title: Conditional Inversion
formula: Had + S + V3, S + would/could/might have + V3
example: Had we left earlier, we would have caught the train.

title: So / Such Inversion
example: So serious was the response to the translation contract that the publication date was reconsidered.

title: It-cleft Sentences
example: It was the national statistics team that presented the sampling methodology, not the outside consultants.

title: Wh-cleft Sentences
example: What the film festival committee needed was a second opinion on the selection criteria.

title: Fronting & Topicalisation
example: The revised syllabus, the school curriculum department reviewed in detail before making a recommendation.

title: Advanced Ellipsis
example: The pharmaceutical review board reviewed the labelling proposal; the external auditors did too.

title: Advanced Substitution
example: The regional tourism board reviewed the visitor-management policy last year and plans to do so again next year.

title: Nominalisation
example: The formal analysis of the rescue coordination plan was completed at the harbour authority office.

title: Complex Noun Phrases
example: The committee circulated a carefully revised version of the quality assurance plan to every department.

title: Apposition
example: The wildlife rehabilitation centre, a non-profit conservation facility, reviewed the release protocol before publication.

title: Mandative Subjunctive
example: The ethics board recommended that the evening event plan be reviewed before implementation.

title: Counterfactual Subjunctive
example: If the workplace mediation service were more transparent about the confidential findings, the public might respond more positively.

title: Advanced Modality
example: Given the latest evidence, the coastal research team may well revise the flood-risk assessment before the vote.

title: Counterfactual Modals
example: The chair confirmed that without additional evidence, the curriculum team would have rejected the assessment rubric.

title: Advanced Non-finite Clauses
example: Having reviewed the air-quality standard, the environment agency issued a recommendation.

title: Absolute Constructions
formula: N + having been + V3, main clause
example: The evidence having been checked, the medicines board issued its findings on the dosage recommendation.

title: Proportional Comparisons
formula: the more ..., the fewer + plural noun
example: The more carefully the accessibility unit checks the interface prototype, the fewer errors it is likely to miss.

title: Advanced Correlative Comparisons
formula: not so much A as B
example: The debate was not so much about the cost of the artefact inventory as about its long-term effects.

title: Advanced Articles & Determiners
example: The inspectors examined the equipment specified in the heritage trail map.

title: Advanced Tense & Aspect
formula: by the time + past, had + V3
example: By the time the hearing began, the water department had already revised the drought response plan twice.

title: Hedging
example: The preliminary figures appear to support the recommendation in the inspection report.

title: Distancing & Evidentiality
formula: It has been reported that + clause
example: It has been reported that the source-protection policy will be revised before publication.

title: Advanced Concession & Qualification
formula: Much as + S + V, main clause
example: Much as the textile cooperative respected the original design, it decided to revise the production proposal.

title: Alternative Conditional Structures
formula: But for + noun, would have + V3
example: But for the additional funding, the weather service would have abandoned the storm-warning bulletin.

title: Academic Cohesion
example: The consultation draft appeared feasible. Nevertheless, the reform committee requested additional testing.

title: Parallelism
formula: to V, to V and to V
example: The wildlife centre agreed to evaluate, to revise and to publish the release protocol according to the same timetable.

title: Extraposition & Anticipatory Subjects
example: It is essential to distinguish observation from interpretation when discussing the recycling guidelines.

title: Punctuation, Scope & Formal Register
example: The committee, however, asked for further evidence before endorsing the shoreline assessment.

title: Subtle Tense Nuances
example: The chair was about to announce the verdict when the alarm sounded.

title: Complex Aspect & Time Reference
example: By the time the inspector arrived, the technicians had been testing the system for six hours.

title: Fine-grained Modality
example: Her signature is on the receipt; she must have signed for the package.

title: Complex Clause Compression
example: Having examined the audit trail, the auditor requested an independent review.

title: Extended Postmodification
example: The audit trail reviewed by the auditor raised further concerns.

title: Idiomatic Discourse Markers
example: The proposal has merits. That said, the unexplained shortfall remains a concern.

title: Spoken Ellipsis & Repairs
example: A: Has the auditor reviewed the audit trail? B: Not yet.

title: Idiomatic Grammar Patterns
example: It is high time the auditor dealt with the unexplained shortfall.

title: Register Shifting
formula: We regret to inform you that
example: We regret to inform you that the unexplained shortfall has delayed the review.

title: Active–Passive Stylistic Choice
example: Before publication, the audit report was reviewed by an independent specialist.

title: Nominal vs Verbal Style
example: To make responsibility clear, the auditor wrote, “We reviewed the audit report yesterday.”

title: Marked Word Order
example: Only later did the compliance committee realise how serious the problem involving the missing signatures was.

title: Information Structure
example: It was the auditor who first pointed out the missing signatures.

title: Ambiguity & Scope
example: The finding that “not all claims in the audit report were verified” means some may remain unverified.

title: Advanced Punctuation
example: the audit report seemed complete; however, the missing signatures remained unresolved.

title: Pragmatic Grammar & Politeness
example: In a formal email, the auditor wrote, “Would it be possible to review the audit report by Thursday?”

title: Expert Editing & Cohesion
example: the compliance committee reviewed the audit report. The document contained several unresolved questions.
